input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new condition stops wrapping string filenames in a tuple, so a single string filename is passed to the editor as an iterable of individual characters. Preserve the string check alongside the new PathLike check.
- rationale: For a call such as edit(filename="notes.txt"), str is not an os.PathLike, so filename reaches edit_files unchanged. Iterating it produces separate filenames such as 'n', 'o', and 't', causing the editor to open the wrong files instead of notes.txt.
critique: The finding describes the same defect as the label. The check tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps str, so a string filename reaches edit_files unchanged and is iterated into single-character filenames, opening the wrong files instead of notes.txt.
